attacks.claim: Vector Store, which holds customer chunks and embeddings, is provisioned only in us-east-2 during public preview, with EU regions unscheduled. Week 2 re-embeds ~41M chunks into it and dual-writes new documents, so customer-derived data leaves the EU in breach of the agreed DPA residency constraint before cutover, not only at it.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." / "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: EU residency is stated only for generation (eu-west-1). The processing location of embed-3 calls, the ingest path, and the Vector Store is not stated, so end-to-end EU-only processing of customer-derived data is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers." ABSENT: region or residency statement for embed-3 or the ingest path.

attacks.claim: Nimbus is a new processor for customer documents, chunks, and embeddings, but the plan contains no DPA amendment, sub-processor notice to customers, transfer mechanism (SCCs/DPF) for the us-east-2 location, or transfer impact assessment.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: DPA/sub-processor update, transfer impact assessment, or customer notification; "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is cited only for the Inference API generation path. The plan does not confirm it covers embed-3 or Vector Store, which persist derived customer data, so retention of embeddings and vectors under the vendor terms is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." ABSENT: ZDR or retention terms for embed-3 and Vector Store.

attacks.claim: The agreed constraint designates the 4,100-case regression suite as the release gate for any model change, but the plan moves it to week 6+, after cutover. The 25-question sample (19 wins, 3 ties) cannot establish 'parity or better' for legal Q&A and does not justify skipping the gate.
attacks.evidence: "The applied team ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox through both stacks... This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly releases the A100 reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters, before the Week 4 cutover and before any regression validation. If Nimbus quality or compliance fails in weeks 4-6, the known-good 70B model cannot be restored, and this also removes the only exit path to a self-hostable model.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle) and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage to close out the 6.2 TB storage line."

attacks.claim: Week 5 removes pgvector, vLLM manifests, and the GPU node pool from Terraform, and the regression suite does not run until week 6+. Rolling back after week 5 means rebuilding the self-hosted stack and re-embedding, so the one-way door is crossed before the release gate has run.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform." / "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: Tenant cutover in week 4 is all-at-once, with no staged or per-tenant rollout, canary, or documented revert trigger. A defect in generation or retrieval affects every law-firm customer simultaneously.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)."

attacks.claim: LoRA-based per-practice behaviour is replaced by drafted system prompts that are not validated against the adapters or the eval suite. Prompt tuning is deferred until after cutover, so behaviour changes reach all tenants before any regression check.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)." / "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: Mid-migration consistency is unaddressed. Old pgvector embeddings and new embed-3 embeddings live in different spaces and cannot be mixed in one index, yet the plan has no reconciliation for the ~41M re-embedded chunks, documents changed or deleted during re-embed, or the query path served during the overlap.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The plan defines no SLOs, alerting, or monitoring for the new Nimbus dependency (latency, errors, 429s, timeouts) before cutover, while the current stack already pages on-call twice a month.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: monitoring, alerting, or SLO section. "Two on-call pages per month trace to vLLM OOMs under long-context load."

attacks.claim: No timeout, retry, backoff, circuit-breaker, or fallback policy is specified for external API calls now on the critical path for both ingest embeddings and query generation/retrieval. Partial failure between generation and Vector Store is unaddressed, and the preview-stage store has no tested failover.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout, retry, backoff, or fallback policy. "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers."

attacks.claim: Re-embedding ~41M chunks shares the rate-limit pool with live query traffic. The plan gives no throughput estimate, batch size, time to completion, or quota split, so backfill could starve production queries or the reverse.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents." ABSENT: embedding throughput, batch size, rate-limit allocation.

attacks.claim: Retrieval latency and recall at ~41M 1,536-dim vectors across many tenant collections are unbenchmarked, yet pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs are removed. The plan includes no query-latency or recall measurement at corpus scale.
attacks.evidence: "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs." ABSENT: vector-store query latency or recall benchmarks at ~41M chunks.

attacks.claim: The latency claim (640 ms vs 910 ms) measures only time-to-first-token for generation, from Frankfurt to Dublin, and excludes the us-east-2 retrieval leg. End-to-end response latency is therefore unsupported.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation is asserted but not demonstrated. The plan does not state that the tenant-scoped key or collection id is derived from the authenticated session rather than request input, and no isolation test is cited for a preview service.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas." ABSENT: server-side enforcement and isolation test results.

attacks.claim: No deletion or erasure path is defined for a tenant's vectors, chunks, or inference logs held by Nimbus on offboarding or DPA-mandated erasure, and vendor-side deletion propagation is unverified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: deletion or erasure procedure for tenant data in Nimbus Vector Store and inference logs.

attacks.claim: No exit or portability plan exists for the 41M-chunk collections or embeddings. embed-3 vectors cannot be used in another index without full re-embedding, and pgvector is deleted in week 5, which makes migrating back costly and creates single-vendor lock-in.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform." ABSENT: data export, re-embedding fallback, or exit-cost estimate.

attacks.claim: The $7,900 generation estimate has no stated token volume, price basis, or per-request budget. Raising context from 32k to 200k makes spend scale with prompt size, and there is no spend ceiling or alerting.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900" / "Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively; our current ceiling is 32k."

attacks.claim: Savings ignore one-time re-embedding cost and the overlap period when both stacks run. The projected monthly delta and payback are therefore overstated, and the Vector Store and embedding line is not broken down or sensitivity-tested for GA pricing.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus embeddings + store | $0 | $1,650" / ABSENT: one-time re-embed cost and overlap cost.
